text.en:
MALACAÑAN PALACE
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES
[ EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 55, September 14, 1936 ]
CREATING A NATIONAL ELECTRICAL-COMMUNICATION BOARD TO ADVISE THE
GOVERNMENT UPON MATTERS PERTAINING TO ELECTRICAL COMMUNICATIONS
WHEREAS, the Constitution of the Philippines prescribes that the State may, in the interest of national
welfare and defense, establish and operate means of transportation and communications; and
WHEREAS, the planning and operation of communication facilities, including telegraph, telephone, and radio
services, should be so coordinated as to insure the utmost economy of public expenditures consistent with
efficiency and national interest and thus avoid unnecessary duplication of such facilities;
NOW, THEREFORE, I, MANUEL L. QUEZON, President of the Philippines, by virtue of the powers in me
vested by law, do hereby constitute and create a National Electrical-Communication Board consisting of—
(1) The Under Secretary of Public Works and Communications, as Chairman; and
(2) A representative from the Philippine Army;
(3) A representative of the Bureau of Posts;
(4) A representative of the Bureau of Public Works; and
(5) A representative of the Government-owned corporations, as members,
